1	<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->
2	
3	## Repo map
4	- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
5	- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
6	- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
7	
8	## Hard invariants
9	- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first. Keep `main` on `main`.
10	- One branch = one concern. If a tangential task appears, commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`.
11	- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
12	- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
13	- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access.
14	- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
15	- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence. If you cannot reproduce, bail and report the dead end.
16	- Run `make pre-pr` (fast no-DB CI gates: typecheck + knip + lint) AND `make review` (LLM verdict) before PR/merge. `make review` does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests — it is not proof CI will pass. If you touch server/runtime code, also run the relevant `bun test`/`make test-integration` suite.
17	- **Run `make review-fix` on the settled diff BEFORE the first `make review`.** It runs the reviewer with write access to fix review-grade findings (bugs, slop, stale claims) without posting a status; verify its diff, commit, then post one review. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle. If a posted review still fails, fix the finding AND its whole class before re-running.
18	- After committing a fix, verify it landed with `git show HEAD:<file>` (or `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`). A fix left in the working tree but never committed will not reach CI — confirm HEAD, not just the working tree.
19	- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.
20	
21	## Agent workflow
22	- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
23	- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
24	- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
25	- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
26	- Subagents that may switch/commit/push/destroy must run in a worktree; read-only research may share the parent.
27	- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
28	- To drive the user's paired Owletto Chrome extension/browser, use `manage_operations` on the active `chrome` connection — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` ("Driving the paired Owletto extension"). Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
29	- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.
30	
31	## Session efficiency
32	- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
33	- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
34	- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change; blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.

---
name: When user identifies a fix, do it — don't save to memory
description: If the user diagnoses the fix in-conversation ("we need to plug X in", "the fix is Y"), execute it via the available APIs; don't record it as project memory
type: feedback
originSessionId: d6d89ea5-39bd-4740-b164-ae0b968030fb
---
When the user says something like "we need to plug in our Google AI OAuth key" or "the fix is X", that is a request for action, not a fact to remember. I over-saved one of these to project memory, which the user called out.

**Why:** Memory is for context that persists across conversations. Identified fixes belong in the codebase / infra as executed changes, not as sticky notes that defer the work.

**How to apply:** When the user names a concrete remediation during a diagnostic session, go straight to the API/CLI/code path to apply it. Only fall back to memory if (a) the user explicitly says "remember this" or (b) the fix can't be executed right now and future-me needs the context.
=====FILE: feedback_batched_no_quality_compromise.md
---
name: feedback_batched_no_quality_compromise
description: "Batch work to save tokens/iterations, but never compromise quality/correctness to do so"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 285a3f95-531f-4921-b227-6c7a2f7e49ef
---

Default to BATCHING work to conserve tokens — but only where it does NOT compromise correctness or quality.

**Why:** the user is token-conscious. Running expensive gates (e.g. the 3-model `make review`) after every single fix is wasteful when fixes are narrow.

**How to apply:**
- For narrow/mechanical fixes, verify locally (tsc + targeted tests) and accumulate several into ONE commit; reserve the full multi-model `make review` for a final confirmation pass, not per-fix.
- When the user says "no need to verify," they mean skip the heavy re-verify (e.g. another full `make review`) — the pre-commit hook (tsc/biome) still runs and that's fine.
- NEVER skip something that would let a real bug through (a red→green reproducer for a bug fix, a correctness-critical test, the final clean review gate). Batching is about cadence/cost, not cutting corners on correctness.
- `pi --no-session` (review.sh) makes every `make review` a fresh stateless re-read of the whole diff — resuming would cost MORE (accumulates history) and bias the review, so don't try to "resume" the review thread to save tokens; instead run it less often.

See [[project_connections_single_table_cutover]] (where 7 full reviews were run; should have batched).

---
name: biome-excludes-packages-server
description: "Never run `biome check --write <file>` on packages/server (or other config-excluded paths) — explicit file args bypass the excludes and reformat whole files (spaces→tabs), bloating the diff"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: e49a880f-0fe7-405d-a6b0-1d062f46e9ec
---

`config/biome.config.json` `files.includes` EXCLUDES `**/packages/server/**`, `**/packages/connector-sdk/**`, and others. The pre-commit hook (`bun run check:fix`) respects this, but invoking `bunx biome check --write <explicit file>` does NOT — it reformats the whole file to tabs/double-quotes, turning a ~400-line semantic diff into ~2900 lines of noise.

**Why:** Biome's includes filtering applies to directory scans, not explicitly-passed file paths.

**How to apply:** To lint/format changed server files, run the repo gate (`bun run check:fix` from root) and let the config decide scope. If biome was accidentally run on an excluded file: `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` and re-apply the semantic edits in the original style (2-space, single quotes for packages/server). Happened on feat/device-watcher-complete-window (2026-06-09).

In the lobu repo, biome must be invoked as `bun run check:fix` (= `biome check --config-path config/biome.config.json --write .`). The config excludes `packages/server/**`, `packages/owletto/**`, connectors, and more — those packages are deliberately NOT biome-formatted.

**Why:** Bare `bunx biome check --write <dir>` uses biome defaults (tab indentation) and reformatted all ~60 files under `packages/server/src/tools` (2026-06-12, tool-arg-validation PR #1234). The repo config then reported "No fixes applied" because the package is excluded — so nothing reverts it; recovery required `git restore` of every tracked file and re-applying the real edits.

**How to apply:** For formatting, run `bun run check:fix` from the repo root (same as the husky pre-commit). Never point biome at `packages/server` directly. Related: `make review` integration step under Node 26 fails on isolated-vm (needs Node 22–24, e.g. `PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"`) and worktree `.env.local` leaks into public-origin/public-pages test expectations — both are environmental, not diff regressions; CI runs Node 22.

=====FILE: feedback_codex_exec_stdin.md
---
name: codex-and-pi-stdin-redirect
description: "Always pipe `< /dev/null` into `codex exec` AND `pi -p` when running them backgrounded or in any non-tty context. Without a tty, both block indefinitely in S state with 0% CPU — they look alive but produce nothing."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: dcbea5b9-f69e-4381-8f21-e51a639075bf
---

Both `codex exec` and `pi -p` (the AI coding-assistant CLIs we lean on for review/dispatch) wait on stdin by default. When invoked via Bash with `run_in_background: true` or in any non-tty context **without** `< /dev/null`, the process blocks in S state at 0% CPU, makes no model API calls, and produces no output — looks "still processing" but is actually hung.

**Affected tools:** every CLI that reads stdin for interactive multiline input. Confirmed: `codex exec`, `pi -p`. Likely: any AI assistant in `--print` / non-interactive mode that still falls back to stdin if it's not closed.

**Symptoms (same for both):**
- Process visible in `ps` as S state, 0:00 CPU time stays flat
- No output written to the redirect target file
- `lsof -p <pid>` shows stdin still open (a tty or /dev/null inherited from parent)
- Burned 29 min waiting on codex, repeated mistake with pi after fixing landing branch — both hung silently

**How to apply:**

Every backgrounded `codex exec`:
```bash
codex exec --config model_reasoning_effort=high "PROMPT" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tail -N
```

Every backgrounded `pi -p`:
```bash
pi -p "PROMPT" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tail -N
```

Round 1 of a session is sometimes lucky (inherited tty from terminal); round 2+ reliably hangs. Don't rely on luck. Treat `< /dev/null` as mandatory for both.

**If you forget:** the process is killable with `kill <pid>`. Re-invoke with `< /dev/null`. Don't waste time troubleshooting the model / network / API key — it's almost always this.

Related: [[feedback_e2e_before_merge]] — the pattern "verify via second tool" only helps if the second tool actually runs.

=====FILE: feedback_e2e_before_merge.md
---
name: feedback-e2e-before-merge
description: "Hard gate — reproduce the failure, apply the fix, reproduce the green path BEFORE opening a PR. Bail if you can't reproduce the original failure."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d6aea831-5800-4c76-ba4b-a9f5c52f04a7
---

**Rule:** before opening a PR for a bug fix, the agent (or me) must do a red → fix → green cycle:

1. Reproduce the failure first (red). Boot PGlite for SQL bugs, the gateway for SSE/runtime bugs, the actual binary for CLI bugs. Capture the error output.
2. Apply the fix.
3. Re-run the reproducer (green). Capture the new output.
4. Paste both in the PR body under a "Reproducer" section.
5. **If you can't reproduce the original failure, BAIL.** Post the dead-end as a comment on the issue. Do not open a PR for a speculative fix.

**Why:** in the 2026-05-17 triage session three PRs (lobu#833, #835, owletto#160) shipped without any e2e validation. #835's pi review explicitly flagged "reproducer not provable from code alone" but it merged anyway because the fix was small and pi-approved. The honest cost: two prod fixes that need 24h of log-watching to confirm they hit the actual smoking gun. Per [[feedback-e2e-verification-required]] (already saved): typecheck+build = compiles, not works.

**Exceptions:** runtime/UI validation on native apps (Mac/iOS) or hardware that needs a human-driven click. **Compile-checks aren't exempt** — `xcodebuild -project … -scheme … -destination "platform=macOS" build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` runs headlessly and catches Swift type errors / missing references / API breakage. If you can't drive the UI, the PR body should say "Compiled clean via xcodebuild; UI flow needs human validation" — not the older "Untested — requires Xcode" which was wrong and skipped the cheap compile-check.

**How to apply:** include the red → fix → green requirement in every dispatch prompt; treat pi approval as necessary-but-not-sufficient. Pi can validate the code shape; only a reproducer validates the *fix*.
=====FILE: feedback_e2e_verification_required.md
---
name: feedback-e2e-verification-required
description: "Never report an implementation as done from typecheck+build alone — boot it against an isolated PGlite DB, exercise every branch + edge case, and emit a confidence score."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b6de651e-8707-4a94-a5a3-7d8e46c618cb
---

Typecheck + `make build-packages` proves the code compiles, NOT that it works. Before reporting a non-trivial change as done, boot the stack against an isolated PGlite database and drive the actual code paths.

**Why:** I claimed "all green" on a connection action_modes refactor after only typecheck/build. User called it out and required actual end-to-end testing, which surfaced real questions about migration backfill, collision handling, and filter behavior — none of which `bun run typecheck` could catch. See AGENTS.md → "IMPORTANT — End-to-end verification before reporting 'done'" section that codifies this.

**How to apply:**
- Boot via the local PGlite entry: `PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH env -u DATABASE_URL PORT=8788 WORKER_PROXY_PORT=8119 LOBU_DATA_DIR=$PWD/.lobu-test-data LOBU_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY=1 node packages/server/dist/start-local.bundle.mjs`. Never against the user's prod or main dev DB. PGlite socket port is in the boot log; psql connects via `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:<port>/postgres?sslmode=disable`. Bootstrap PAT is printed once + saved to `<LOBU_DATA_DIR>/bootstrap-pat.txt`.
- Edge cases are mandatory: migrations need backfill + collision + `migrate:down` round-trip; filters need positive + negative + the should-NOT-filter case; every enum branch gets one execution.
- Report a confidence score (0–100) per surface, plus an explicit list of what's unverified. If you didn't boot it, say so — don't dress a typecheck up as verification.
- Clean up afterward: kill the test server PID, `rm -rf` the test data dir, delete any `/tmp/*` scratch files.

Related: [[feedback-action-vs-memory]] (execute fixes, don't journal them).

> Pre-trim index line (2026-06-12, full detail preserved): - [E2E verification before "done"](feedback_e2e_verification_required.md) — Typecheck+build = compiles, not works. Boot PGlite (`start-local.bundle.mjs` + `LOBU_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY=1`, isolated `LOBU_DATA_DIR`), drive every branch + edge case (migrations: backfill+collision+down; filters: pos+neg+un-scoped), emit a confidence score per surface.

name: feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class
description: "On a repeated root cause, generalize the fix and grep the whole class in ONE pass — don't iterate an adversarial diff-review one cited line at a time (PR2 took 7 rounds for ~3 real defects)"
metadata:

---

PR2 (feat/agent-models-list) took SEVEN Codex gpt-5.6-sol rounds to clear. Most rounds were rediscovery of ONE defect class: "an agent-scoped DB read must be org-scoped or fail closed for an orgless shared-id worker token." It re-manifested on the model read (R5), skills read (R6), instruction + MCP reads (R6/R7), and finally the Slack platform-instructions provider `listConnections` (R7) — the same root cause found ~4 times because each round I fixed only the exact line Codex cited, and a diff-scoped reviewer always finds the NEXT nearest instance, never "there's a whole class here."

**Why:** Codex/pi review the diff you hand them. Narrow fix → next review finds the next instance. LLM review is good at "is this a real bug" (verdict) and bad+slow at "did you get all N instances" (coverage). I conflated the two and paid ~2h wall-clock + ~800k tokens/round for content that was ~3 rounds of distinct signal.

**How to apply:**
1. On the FIRST BLOCK of a class, generalize the fix directive: don't say "guard line X," say "audit EVERY sibling of this pattern in the file/module and fix them all in one pass."
2. Front-load a whole-class grep BEFORE the review loop for invariant-heavy PRs (security/tenant-isolation): enumerate every call site of the pattern (e.g. every `getSettings(`, `listConnections(`, `WHERE a.id=`) reachable on the surface. That upfront pass is the round that matters; the rest is rediscovery.
3. Use the reviewer for the VERDICT, grep for the COVERAGE. Don't ask an LLM to walk you through instances one file at a time.
4. Cap-and-escalate rule: if TWO consecutive rounds find variants of the same root cause, STOP iterating and grep-enumerate the class instead of running another review round.
5. Batch the fixes: send all class instances + any genuinely-separate finding in ONE dispatch, not one per round.

Relates to [[feedback_use_fable_for_review]] and [[feedback_no_dynamic_workflows]] (review inline, mind token cost).

name: feedback_make_review_base_in_worktree
description: "In a task-setup worktree, run make review with BASE=origin/main — local main ref is stale and reviews unrelated history"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 56c0e43e-b690-467a-a4ec-42067d87cffd
---

In a `make task-setup` worktree, run `make review BASE=origin/main`, not bare `make review`.

**Why:** `scripts/review.sh` defaults `BASE=main` (the *local* ref). task-setup leaves local `main` pinned at the session-start commit, so it drifts behind `origin/main` as PRs merge. The merge-base then lands way back, and pi reviews every unrelated change that landed on main since the branch point — producing a bogus verdict full of "bugs/blockers" in files you never touched. Burned 2026-05-25 on PR #1051 (a 1-file CI YAML change): bare `make review` reported bug_free 45 / 4 bugs / 2 blockers across 150 files (connection-token-route.ts, desired-state.ts, prometheusrule.yaml…); `BASE=origin/main` gave the true verdict bug_free 92 / 0 bugs / 0 blockers.

**How to apply:** Always `make review BASE=origin/main` from a worktree (fetches+diffs against the real base). If a verdict flags files outside your diff, you used the stale base — re-run with `BASE=origin/main`. Connects to [[feedback_verify_query_plan]] (verify the review agent's claims against the actual diff before trusting them).

---
name: merge-main-conflict-resolution
description: "Don't resolve \"Merge main into branch\" conflicts in GitHub's web UI — it silently reverts feature work. Use rebase or a verified local merge."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 5bf00915-b9ca-4364-8c86-bac086a8e130
---

When syncing main into a feature branch, never resolve conflicts through GitHub's web conflict editor or any "accept current/incoming" UI without a follow-up diff check. Prefer `git rebase main` locally, or if a merge is unavoidable, run `git diff <feature-branch-tip> HEAD` after resolving and verify no feature files lost lines.

**Why:** In May 2026 the squash-merge of `feat/connectors-mcp-agents-ux` (web PR #118) silently dropped ~1300 lines of feature work — entire new files (`clients.tsx`, `feed-expanded-row.tsx`), a redesigned connector picker (4-col grid + auth chips), and a panels refactor. Root cause: the `Merge main into feat/connectors-mcp-agents-ux` commit (`deb2a82`) resolved conflicts in a way that picked main's side for every file the branch was actively rewriting. The squash that landed (`2efbd87`) inherited the already-broken tree. Recovered in web PR #121 + #122 and parent PRs #741 + #742.

**How to apply:**
- Before pressing "squash and merge" on a PR whose head is a merge commit (`Merge main into ...`), compare the merge's tree against the last *real* feature commit: `git diff <feature-tip-before-merge> <merge-head> -- <feature-touched-files>`. Any large `-` delta on files the branch added or rewrote is a red flag.
- When auditing past PRs for similar losses: `git log --grep "Merge main into\|Merge branch 'main'"` flags candidates. Cross-check whether each merge ended up on main (`git branch -a --contains <sha>`).
- Prefer `git rebase main` over merging main in for short-lived feature branches — rebases force per-commit conflict resolution, where mistakes are smaller and easier to see.

Always use static `import` statements. Do NOT introduce `await import(...)` calls.

**Why:** Dynamic imports hide failures behind `try/catch`, defeat tree-shaking, and turn module-load wiring bugs into late-binding runtime warnings. The user explicitly called this out as unreliable when reviewing the identity-engine wiring in `auth/index.tsx`.

**How to apply:**
- For module hooks (e.g. BetterAuth `databaseHooks`), import the handler at the top of the file and call it directly.
- For side-effect registries (e.g. `connectors/index.ts`), use a static `import './connectors'` so registration happens at module load. Add a startup assertion in the registry's index file (e.g. `if (registry.size() === 0) throw`) so a missed import fails loud at boot, not at first request.

############ packages/server/AGENTS.md (      53 lines)
# Server package agent rules

Read root `AGENTS.md` first. This package owns the gateway, auth, connections, feeds, orchestration, connector operations, guardrails, Slackbot MCP integration, and embedded runtime.

## Boundaries and vocabulary
- Connections are rows, not processes. Agents bind to connections/channels; replicas hydrate connection instances on demand from DB rows and must not assume boot warm-start.
- Connectors collect external data into feeds/events; chat platforms deliver conversations/messages. Do not blur connector sync with chat transport.
- Behaviors are the UI umbrella: Listen, Watch, Schedule. A watcher owns windows; a window's living state is a canvas (`semantic_type='canvas_state'`). Artifacts are stored files, not watcher state.
- Platform isolation: InteractionService events carry `platform`; each renderer filters on its own platform and never another's.

## Connections, feeds, and routing
- Chat platforms live under `src/gateway/connections/` and use Chat SDK adapters. Configure connections via `/agents` UI or CRUD API; do not add per-platform env vars or bespoke SDK transports.
- Webhooks are the default transport. Telegram alone supports `auto|webhook|polling`; reject polling in cloud mode.
- `feeds` is the unified list. `kind='collected'` feeds are scheduled connector pulls into `events`; `kind='streaming'` feeds are chat channels backed by `channel_messages`, not scheduled syncs; `virtual` feeds are projections/metadata and must not be queued as real sync work.
- Runtime connection ids may be slugs/managed ids (for example `slackinst-…`), not numeric `connections.id`. Resolve through connection stores; do not cast runtime ids to bigint.
- Bound chat channels should materialize an idempotent streaming feed so the UI has one feed model, not a separate channel island.

## Auth, providers, and secrets
- Product auth uses better-auth/session/PAT flows in `src/auth`; model/provider auth and user auth profiles live under `src/gateway/auth`.
- Provider catalog/settings are org/user scoped. Do not hardcode provider credentials, base URLs, or model lists; resolve through the provider catalog/settings stores.
- Workers never see real credentials. The gateway secret/MCP proxies swap placeholders or inject OAuth/API credentials at egress.
- MCP servers come from per-agent settings or `SKILL.md`; workers discover tools at startup and call them through the gateway proxy.
- Device-pinned connectors are special: resolved connection credentials may be delivered only to the authorized device worker that owns that run.

## Multi-replica correctness
- Production can run N>1 replicas behind ClientIP affinity. Before claiming a feature works, ask: “does this hold with 3 replicas?”
- Per-pod state (`SseManager`, event backlog, in-process worker map, deploy-lock cache) is pod-local. Cross-replica delivery must use Postgres (`thread_response` queue or equivalent).
- API/SSE terminal rows and interaction cards are owner-routed; non-owners requeue until the owning pod claims. Headless rows with no SSE client may be delivered by first claim.
- Streaming deltas/status are best-effort across pods today. Do not build correctness on cross-pod in-memory delivery.
- Exclusive transports such as Telegram polling run on exactly one replica via `connection_claims`; webhook transports must run on any replica.

## Connector operations and repair
- Built-in connector definitions/catalog install in server; connector implementation details belong in `packages/connectors/AGENTS.md`.

## Boundaries

# Gotchas

Traps that have each cost a real debugging session. Read the section for the surface you are touching before you start; each entry is written as a symptom you would actually see, so grep this file when something looks inexplicable.

Root `AGENTS.md` holds the invariants and the workflow. This file holds the mechanical failure modes.

## Build & typecheck

**Stale dist gives a false green typecheck.** `packages/server` typechecks against the *built* `dist` of `@lobu/core`, not its source. If you change a `@lobu/core` contract and only run `make typecheck`, the green is meaningless. Run `make build-packages` first on any PR touching core contracts, and never `--admin`-merge past a typecheck check that has not reported.

**Phantom `TS2305: Module '@lobu/core' has no exported member 'X'` inside a worktree.** The worktree's own `@lobu/*` dists are missing, so tsc resolves through the *main checkout's* stale dist. Build the worktree's dists (`make build-packages`). `packages/core` is `composite: true`, so use `bunx tsc --build --force` — a plain `rm -rf dist` leaves a stale `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` behind. Diagnose with `bunx tsc --noEmit --traceResolution 2>&1 | grep "@lobu/core"`.

**A new workspace package must be added to three build lists or CI fails while local passes.** In dependency order: the `build-packages` loop in `Makefile`, the unit job's inline build step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (it builds packages individually, not via make), and `build:packages` in the root `package.json`. Symptom is `TS2307: Cannot find module '@lobu/<pkg>'` cascading into implicit-any noise. Reproduce locally with `rm -rf packages/<pkg>/dist` then typecheck.

**Inter-package deps are always `"@lobu/*": "workspace:*"`.** Never a hardcoded version or caret range — the root `package.json` is the single source of version truth.

**In a fresh worktree, `git submodule update --init` before `bun install`.** Without the submodule present, bun silently prunes the workspace importer out of `bun.lock`. If you touched no dependencies, `bun.lock` must come back unchanged — if it didn't, you hit this.

## Formatting & lint

**Format only via `bun run check:fix` from the repo root.** Never `bunx biome check --write <path>`. Bare biome uses its own defaults (tabs) and ignores the repo config at `config/biome.config.json`.

**Several packages are biome-EXCLUDED, and an explicit file argument bypasses the exclusion.** `config/biome.config.json` excludes `packages/server`, `packages/owletto`, connector-sdk, connectors, connector-worker, embeddings, openclaw-plugin, apps, and skills. Running biome on a file in one of them turns a 400-line semantic diff into thousands of lines of reflow noise that biome will not undo and the CI format check will not catch. Recover with `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` and redo the edit by hand in the file's existing style (2-space, single quotes). `packages/core` and `packages/cli` *are* biome-formatted.

## DB & SQL

**Never bind a raw JS array as a query parameter in `packages/server`.** The client sets `fetch_types: false` (`PROD_PG_VALUE_OPTIONS` in `packages/server/src/db/client.ts`), so postgres.js ships arrays as scalars and you get `PostgresError: malformed array literal`. This holds for `number[]` and `string[]`, tagged-template and `sql.unsafe`, with or without an `::type[]` cast. Safe forms only:

```ts
sql`... WHERE id = ANY(${pgTextArray(ids)}::text[])`     // strings
sql`... WHERE id = ANY(${pgBigintArray(ids)}::bigint[])` // numbers
```

`sql.array(a)`, `ARRAY[$a, $b]` of scalars, and spreads are also safe. JSONB is exempt (`JSON.stringify` / `sql.json`). CI enforces this via `scripts/check-raw-array-params.mjs`; the escape hatch is a `raw-array-ok` line comment.

**pgvector columns read back as the text string `"[1,2,3]"`, not `number[]`.** Parse before use.

**Reproduce array-binding bugs with `getDb()`, not `getTestDb()`.** Both share the prod value options, but test-client type inference can mask the failure you are chasing.

**Dropping a column from a queryable table is a two-phase change.** `buildScopedQuery` emits explicit column lists from `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA`, so a single-release drop breaks old replicas mid-rollout. Remove the column from `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` in release N; ship the `DROP COLUMN` migration in release N+1.

**New migrations are lock-safety linted by squawk in CI, and it exits non-zero on warnings.** The `migrations` job runs `squawk-cli` (version pinned in both `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the `db:lint` script) over only the changed `db/migrations/*.sql`. Note `make review` does *not* run it. Conventions: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; fold unique indexes into a table-level `CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE`; a non-unique index on a brand-new table needs `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` plus `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; a `migrate:down` DROP needs `-- squawk-ignore ban-drop-table`. Check locally with `bun run db:lint db/migrations/<file>.sql`.

**After `dbmate up` + `normalize-schema.sh`, hand-patch `schema_migrations.version` back to `character varying(128)`** before committing `db/schema.sql`. Local `pg_dump` strips the length and the CI drift check fails.

**Read the actual SQL before scoping performance work.** A review agent claiming "JSONB full scan" is a claim, not a measurement — a PK-anchored JSONB extract is microseconds. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before you denormalize anything.

## Testing

**Hoisted `vi.mock()` silently fails in the server *integration* suite.** That run shares a module registry across files, so a test that is green alone loads the real module in CI. Use `vi.resetModules()` + `vi.doMock(...)` + a dynamic `await import()` *after* the mock, with an `afterEach` that resets modules and un-mocks. Always verify by co-running siblings — `vitest run <fileA> <fileB>` — because green-alone is not green-in-suite.

**Running the server integration suite locally** needs Node 22 (the repo rejects newer), and `@lobu/pgvector-embedded` must be built first (`cd packages/pgvector-embedded && bun run build`) or global setup dies with `ERR_RESOLVE_PACKAGE_ENTRY_FAIL`. Global setup uses `DATABASE_URL` if set, otherwise spawns an ephemeral embedded Postgres + pgvector. On macOS, `could not create shared memory segment: No space left on device` is the SHMMNI limit — reap detached segments with `ipcs -mob`, then `ipcrm -m <id>` for entries with `nattch=0` only.

**`make dev` is not the test harness.** It only schema-version-*checks*; it never migrates. Pre-migrate with `dbmate --no-dump-schema --migrations-dir db/migrations up`.

**Isolating a benchmark/scratch server:** pass `DATABASE_URL="file:///tmp/<dir>"` — the embedded runtime creates `<dir>/.lobu/pgdata`. `LOBU_DATA_DIR` is *not* honored, and without `DATABASE_URL` you silently share `~/.lobu/pgdata`. Kill orphans by port, not name: `pkill -f "lobu run --port"` never matches, because the real cmdline is `node .../server.bundle.mjs`. Use `lsof -tiTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill -9`. A fresh initdb plus migrations takes ~15s, so "healthy after 2s" means you are talking to an orphan.

## Shell & CLI

**Always append `< /dev/null` to `codex exec` and `pi -p`** in any non-tty or background invocation. Without it they block in `S` state at 0% CPU and silently produce nothing.

**macOS `/bin/sh` is bash 3.2 and mis-parses a heredoc nested inside `"$(cat <<'DELIM' … DELIM)"`.** A single apostrophe in the body kills the script with `unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`. Never inline user- or server-controlled text into a generated shell script that way — write it to a `0600` tempfile and read it back with `"$(cat '<file>')"` at runtime. Validate generated scripts with `/bin/sh -n`, not interactive zsh.

## Browser & connectors

**`"Playwright not installed or Chromium browser missing"` is a mislabel.** `packages/connector-sdk/src/browser/launcher.ts` conflates "executable doesn't exist" with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and it is almost always the path. Two things must hold: `docker/worker/Dockerfile` and `docker/app/Dockerfile` set `ENV PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright` *before* install (otherwise chromium lands in `$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright`, the root app pod succeeds, the uid-1001 worker pod fails, and it reads as "intermittent"); and because `playwright` is aliased to patchright in `package.json` while `node_modules/.bin/playwright` is vanilla, install via `node node_modules/playwright/cli.js install chromium` so the install revision matches the runtime revision. In-pod check:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright node -e "const p=require('playwright').chromium.executablePath();console.log(p, require('fs').existsSync(p))"
```

**Connector success status in `runs` is `completed`, not `success`.** Nudge a feed with `UPDATE feeds SET next_run_at = now() WHERE id = …`.

**To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension**, not claude-in-chrome (that drives a different Chrome without their sessions) and not `lobu connector run` (local Playwright/CDP only — it errors with "Missing --auth-profile"). The recipe is in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` under "Driving the paired Owletto extension"; it routes through `packages/server/src/worker-api/dispatch-chrome-action.ts`. Note that `search_sdk` does not list the `operations` namespace — discover it via `run_sdk` with `Object.keys(client)`. A new server-side chrome action also needs a handler in the *installed* extension build, so check `git ls-tree origin/main packages/owletto`, never the working-tree submodule HEAD.

**Receiving real third-party webhooks against a local gateway** uses Tailscale Funnel on :443: `tailscale funnel --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. The `serve` subcommand looks identical but silently makes the port tailnet-only — always `funnel`, and verify with `tailscale funnel status`. curl from the same machine resolves over the tailnet, so a local 200 does not prove public reachability.

## Submodule & cross-repo

**Never point the parent repo at a submodule SHA that is unreachable from the submodule's remote.** Push the submodule first, then bump the pointer. Prod submodule clones fail on unreachable SHAs.

**Landing paired lobu + owletto PRs:** merge the owletto PR (squash), take the resulting owletto-main SHA, re-point the lobu submodule pointer PR at *that squash SHA*, then merge lobu. `check-drift` fails until the pointer is an ancestor of owletto/main. When the pointer branch is behind lobu main, use `git merge origin/main` — **never `git rebase`**, which drops the pointer commit as "patch contents already upstream", after which a `--amend` corrupts HEAD. Recover with `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`, then merge and resolve the single submodule conflict:

```sh
git -C packages/owletto checkout <squash-sha> && git add packages/owletto && git commit --no-edit
```

**Never fold a private repo into public `lobu`.** Check `gh repo view --json visibility` on both sides before any "consolidate into the monorepo" move — a past fold leaked a large private frontend publicly.

## Prod safety

**Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows,** including zero-activity ones. Empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.

**Before testing run/sync flows locally against a shared prod database, scale the prod worker deployment to 0** and restore it afterwards. Otherwise the prod worker pod claims your pending runs and fails them out from under local dev.

# Connector SDK package agent rules

Read root `AGENTS.md` first. This package is the contract every connector compiles against: `ConnectorRuntime`, the source primitives (`file-source`, `acl-source`, `http-client`), identity normalization, pagination/retry/scoring helpers, and the browser automation layer. Connector *implementations* live in `packages/connectors` — keep this package generic.

## Boundaries
- This is a published contract consumed by external connectors. A breaking change to an exported type or runtime method breaks compiled connectors in the wild — additive changes only unless a migration is planned.
- `playwright` is a **peer** dependency aliased to patchright, and it is optional. Never make a top-level import of it a hard requirement of the package entrypoint; browser code must stay reachable only from the browser paths.
- Egress helpers enforce SSRF guards and domain allowlists (`url-guards.ts`). Route new outbound-fetch surfaces through them rather than calling `fetch` directly.

## Browser automation
- The stealth layer exists to look like a real browser; patchright (not vanilla playwright) is deliberate. Do not "fix" the alias in `package.json` — install revision and runtime revision must match, or Chromium fails to launch.
- `launcher.ts` distinguishes two failure modes: a `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` mismatch versus an unresolvable package. When a launch fails, read which error you got before debugging — see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Browser & connectors", for the Docker/install invariants behind it.
- CDP (`cdp.ts`, `cdp-page.ts`) and the extension scrape paths (`extension-dom-scrape.ts`, `extension-network.ts`) are different backends with different auth stories. Extension paths reach the user's real logged-in sessions; local Playwright/CDP does not.

- This package is **biome-excluded** (`config/biome.config.json`). Never run biome on it — edit surgically, matching each file's existing style. See `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Formatting & lint".
- Adding this package to another package's imports means adding it to all three build lists — see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Build & typecheck".

## Validation
- Validation: the root gates (`make pre-pr` + `make review`, see root `AGENTS.md`) plus targeted SDK tests. Browser changes need a real connector run, not just a unit test — a green mock proves nothing about Chromium launch.

Read root `AGENTS.md` first. This package holds the shared contracts every other package builds against: types, errors, capabilities, credentials, the guardrail engine, and the logger. Ten workspace packages depend on it.

- Core is the bottom of the dependency graph. It must not import from `server`, `agent-worker`, `connectors`, or any package above it — if a helper needs one of those, it does not belong here.

- **After any contract change, rebuild before trusting a typecheck.** A stale `dist` produces a green typecheck that CI then fails, and inside a worktree it produces phantom `TS2305` errors resolved from the main checkout's dist. `make pre-pr` builds first for exactly this reason. See `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Build & typecheck".
- This package is `composite: true`, so use `bunx tsc --build --force` to force a rebuild. A plain `rm -rf dist` leaves a stale `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` behind and the next build no-ops.
- Unlike `server` and `connector-sdk`, this package **is** biome-formatted — use `bun run check:fix` from the repo root.

## Validation
- Validation: the root gates (`make pre-pr` + `make review`, see root `AGENTS.md`). For a contract change, also typecheck the consumers — a green build here says nothing about the ten packages downstream.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.

- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. Batching is about cadence and cost; it never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Tree clean, three commits, gates green. Everything asked for is done.

## What landed

All four items, on branch `feat/agent-docs-port` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-docs-port`), 3 commits, working tree clean:

**1. Proper branch** — moved off `chore/peek-seed-and-submodule`; the main checkout is back to clean.

**2. Cold-read test** — a fresh agent given *only* these docs answered 5 of 7 onboarding questions confidently. The two failures drove real fixes: there was **no push/PR/merge step documented anywhere**, and **no way to run a single test** — so the mandated red→fix→green evidence was literally unfollowable from the docs. Both now exist as a numbered `## Ship a change` flow.

**3. New package docs** — `packages/core/AGENTS.md` and `packages/connector-sdk/AGENTS.md`, plus traps moved to the top of `packages/server/AGENTS.md` so a skimming agent hits the destructive warnings before the glossary.

**4. `BASE=origin/main`** — not enforced, **deleted**. `review.sh:64-68` already defaults to `origin/main` with a comment explaining the exact worktree-staleness problem. The memory that generated that rule was stale; the code had fixed it.

## Corrections found along the way

Verification kept beating recollection. Nine claims sourced from memory or existing docs turned out to be wrong:

- `db/schema.sql` + `normalize-schema.sh` — files don't exist; ci.yml:808 says the drift gate was deliberately removed
- `launcher.ts` "mislabels the error" — already fixed, distinguishes both cases precisely
- `createLogger` drops metadata — already fixed
- "repo rejects Node newer than 22" — actually accepts 22–24 and 26+ (`lobu.js:30`)
- `HTTP_PROXY=localhost:8118` — reads `WORKER_PROXY_PORT`; 8118 is a fallback
- `openclaw-plugin` biome exclusion — gone
- "`search_sdk` doesn't list operations" — it does; `connector-discovery.ts:154` routes agents there
- `make pre-pr` runs 4 steps — runs 5; step 5 enforces a Behavior-vs-`watcher` naming rule agents need
- `packages/connectors` uses `*.connector.ts` — built-ins are plain `.ts`; that suffix is for user-authored connectors

Also fixed the PR template, which pointed at an AGENTS.md section that no longer exists.

## Gates

`make pre-pr` clean (5/5). `make review-fix` ran and made corrections across 7 files — I verified each against the tree before committing rather than trusting it, which is how items 4–8 above were confirmed. The 2 biome infos are pre-existing, in files I never touched.

## Confidence: 90

Basis: every added claim was grepped against the working tree; the fixer's corrections were independently re-verified, not accepted; a cold agent actually read the result. The gap: the Tailscale-funnel and Docker/Playwright recipes are infra-side — I confirmed the referenced files and env vars exist, not that the procedures still work end-to-end.

## Next actions

1. **`make review` and open the PR** — step 8-9 of the flow I just documented. I stopped short since pushing is outward-facing.
2. Prune the 3 disproven memories from local memory (logger drop, no-Sheets, `BASE=origin/main`) so they don't regenerate bad docs.
3. Re-verify the infra recipes next time you're in a pod — the one unverified surface.

# CLI package agent rules

Read root `AGENTS.md` first. This package is the `lobu` binary users install from npm: commands, project templates, config resolution, and the bundled server the Owletto Mac app shells out to.

## Boundaries
- This is a published user-facing binary. Error messages are product surface — write them for someone who has never read this repo, and keep the agent-facing vocabulary rule (**Behavior**, never `watcher`) in anything a user or agent sees.
- `bin/lobu.js` runs on whatever Node the user has, *before* the bundle loads. Keep it dependency-free and import-free; anything it needs must be inline.
- The installed Mac app invokes the global `lobu` on PATH and runs the frozen `dist`, so a source edit is invisible until the package is rebuilt.

## Package-specific traps
- **The dynamic import in `bin/lobu.js` is required — do not "fix" it to a static import.** A static import is hoisted and evaluated before the Node-version gate runs, so an unsupported Node would load the bundle and throw a cryptic error instead of the friendly message. This is a deliberate, documented exception to the repo's static-import rule.
- Node support is 22–24 and 26+ (25 boots without the SDK sandbox). The gate in `bin/lobu.js` is the single source of that truth — update it there, not in prose.
- This package **is** biome-formatted — use `bun run check:fix` from the repo root.
- `packages/cli` builds last in every build list because it bundles the others; a new workspace package it depends on must be added *before* it. See `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Build & typecheck".

## Validation
- Validation: the root gates (`make pre-pr` + `make review`, see root `AGENTS.md`) plus targeted CLI tests. Changing command output or the version gate needs a real invocation — run the built binary, not just the unit test.

## Submodule & cross-repo

**Never point the parent repo at a submodule SHA that is unreachable from the submodule's remote.** Push the submodule first, then bump the pointer. Prod submodule clones fail on unreachable SHAs.

**Landing paired lobu + owletto PRs:** merge the owletto PR (squash), take the resulting owletto-main SHA, re-point the lobu submodule pointer PR at *that squash SHA*, then merge lobu. `check-drift` fails until the pointer is an ancestor of owletto/main. When the pointer branch is behind lobu main, use `git merge origin/main` — **never `git rebase`**, which drops the pointer commit as "patch contents already upstream", after which a `--amend` corrupts HEAD. Recover with `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`, then merge and resolve the single submodule conflict:

## What `isolated-vm` actually is

`isolated-vm` runs the MCP `execute` tool's user JS inside a V8 isolate with hard caps (64 MB / 60 s / 200 SDK calls / 1 MB output). The package is in maintenance mode and has had RCE-class issues historically (CVE-2022-39266 on ≤4.3.6 via untrusted V8 cached data). Upstream itself recommends a multi-process architecture for hostile code. Pin to the latest patched version, but do not lean on V8 isolates as the only boundary.

## Network egress

Workers run with `HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:8118`. The gateway's in-process proxy enforces:
- **Allowlist mode** — only configured domains reachable.
- **Blocklist mode** — allow all except denied domains.
- **LLM egress judge** — risky domains get LLM verdict per request, with a 5 min cache and a circuit breaker.

In embedded mode, `HTTP_PROXY` is **advisory** at the language layer — a worker process that explicitly bypasses the env var can `connect()` directly. On Linux production hosts, the worker spawn path uses `systemd-run --user --scope` with `IPAddressDeny=any` + `IPAddressAllow=127.0.0.1` so the kernel drops anything that isn't going to the local proxy. On macOS dev hosts there is no kernel-level enforcement.

## Worker process hardening (Linux)

When `systemd-run` is available on the host, `EmbeddedDeploymentManager` wraps each worker spawn in a transient unit with:

- `NoNewPrivileges=yes`
- `PrivateTmp=yes`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome=yes`, `ReadWritePaths=<workspace>`
- `MemoryMax=512M`, `CPUQuota=200%`, `TasksMax=64`, `LimitNOFILE=1024`
- `IPAddressDeny=any`, `IPAddressAllow=127.0.0.1`
- `CapabilityBoundingSet=` (drop all)
- `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6` (no `AF_PACKET` / raw sockets)

This closes most of the gap between "subprocess on the same host" and what Docker namespaces gave us. Recommended for any production deployment on Linux.

This changes the picture materially. The code comment at lines 206-215 explains why the hardening was deliberately *removed*, not overlooked:

- A `--scope` **adopts** an already-forked process, so systemd never execs it and physically cannot apply exec-context hardening. Strict systemd (255) rejects each property with "Unknown assignment" and **the whole scope fails — the worker dies before it starts.**
- Applying them requires `--service`, which would detach the worker from the gateway's process tree and **break stdout/stderr piping and group-signal teardown.**

So "restore the hardening" isn't a config tweak — it's a re-architecture of worker lifecycle management, with a known failure mode. Let me confirm the tests agree.

Memory pruning is done and merged into your local memory. I did **not** do the hardening change, because investigating it showed the premise was wrong — including my own framing of it last turn.

## Done: memory pruning

- **Deleted** `feedback_make_review_base_in_worktree.md` — `review.sh:64-68` already defaults to `origin/main`. Removed its MEMORY.md line.
- **Corrected** the logger memory rather than deleting it — section 1 (metadata drop) is fixed and now says so explicitly; sections 2–3 (the App Home bug record and the reusable prod Slack debug recipe) are still valid.
- **Corrected** the no-Sheets memory — the *rule* is still live design policy, but the migration is complete (zero `components/ui/sheet` callsites) and the path moved `packages/web` → `packages/owletto`. Deleting it would have lost a standing preference.
- **Added** `project_agent_docs_ported_to_repo.md` so future sessions know the repo docs are now source of truth for repo mechanics.

A hook fired mid-edit: MEMORY.md had grown to 20KB against a 24.4KB read limit — past that, the index silently stops loading and *every* memory becomes invisible. Compacted to **16.5KB**, verified independently: 149/149 entries intact, identical link set, every target file exists.

## Not done: systemd hardening — and you should know why

You approved this based on my framing, and my framing was incomplete. Reading the spawn path properly:

**The hardening was never implemented, and cannot be with the current design.** `git log -S "NoNewPrivileges=yes"` returns nothing — no commit ever had it. `docs/SECURITY.md` described an aspiration, not a regression.

The code comment (`deployment-manager.ts:206-215`) explains why:

- A `--scope` **adopts** a process the caller already forked, so systemd never execs it and physically cannot apply exec-context properties. Strict systemd (observed on 255) rejects each with "Unknown assignment" and **the entire scope fails — the worker dies before it starts.**
- Applying them needs `--service`, which detaches the worker from the gateway's process tree and **breaks stdout/stderr piping and group-signal teardown.**

There's a regression test at `orchestration-harden.test.ts:311-319` asserting those properties stay absent, with the comment *"or the whole scope fails and the worker dies."*

So implementing what you approved would have broken worker spawn on every Linux host. I stopped and cleaned up the worktree rather than ship it.

**The docs are already correct** — PR #2197 landed the accurate description (`--scope` can apply cgroup + network properties, *cannot* apply exec-context controls). Nothing is currently misstated.

## Confidence: 94

Basis: read the full spawn path, the explanatory comment, the regression test, and searched git history for the property. Four independent sources agree. The 6%: I can't execute the Linux systemd path from macOS, so I'm trusting the comment's claim about systemd 255's rejection behavior rather than reproducing it.

## Your actual options

This is a real gap — workers get cgroup + loopback-only networking, but no capability drops or filesystem protection. Worth deciding deliberately:

1. **Accept it and move on.** Single-tenant threat model; `docs/SECURITY.md` now states the boundary honestly. Zero work.
2. **Open an issue** documenting the scope-vs-service tradeoff so it's tracked rather than rediscovered. I can write it up.
3. **Do the `--service` migration** as a real project — it needs a new lifecycle design for stdout/stderr and teardown, plus E2E on an actual Linux host. Not something to merge from here.
4. **Push isolation down a layer** — per-tenant VM/gVisor/Firecracker at deployment, which `docs/SECURITY.md` already recommends for hostile-code threat models.

I'd suggest 2 as the cheap next step. Say the word and I'll file it.
